_comment: Corrections applied to Hevy's published OpenAPI document. Each patch asserts what it expects to find, so a patch that stops matching means upstream changed and the correction needs re-checking rather than silently reapplying. See reference/observed.md for how each was verified.

patches.why: Upstream declares the scheme but no 401 on any operation, and this 401 is not JSON. Observed 2026-08-22, re-checked on all 24 operations 2026-11-18.

value.description: A personal key, issued at https://developers.hevy.com/api-key to Hevy Pro accounts. A missing or wrong key returns 401 with the plain-text body InvalidApiKey served as text/html, not JSON.

patches.why: A wrong bearer token answers 401 as JSON, a different shape from the api-key 401, and upstream documents neither. Observed 2026-11-18 with an invalid token; no valid token was exercised.

value.description: An OAuth access token from https://hevy.com/api/token, valid for one hour. A wrong or expired token returns 401 with {"message": "Invalid or expired token"} as application/json.

patches.why: Every body measurement carries an integer id the spec omits. It is not accepted on write.

value.description: Server-assigned id. Absent from the spec, and rejected by PUT.

patches.why: Returned alongside id, and equally undocumented.

The spec defaults since to the epoch, but omitting it returns nothing: 0 events and page_count 1 on an account with hundreds of workouts, observed 2026-08-23. Whether the server substitutes a recent default or matches nothing was not determined. The false default is dropped so a generated client sends since explicitly.
PUT /v1/workouts/{workoutId} wraps its response the same way as the create. Observed 2026-08-23 and again 2026-11-18.

workout.description: The updated workout, as the array's only element.

patches.why: The spec marks rep_range nullable on a routine update, and a read returns null for a set without one. Sending that null back answers 400, "Expected object, received null". An object whose start and end are null is accepted and reads back as null. Observed 2026-11-18 on PUT only: the create route was not sent a null.
POST /v1/routine_folders returns {"routine_folder": {...}}, wrapped in a key but not in an array. Observed 2026-08-23 and again 2026-11-18.
POST /v1/exercise_templates answers with the new template's UUID as bare text under text/html, not the {"id": <integer>} the spec declares. Observed 2026-08-23 and again 2026-11-18.

id.description: The ID of the exercise template

schema.description: The new template's id as bare text: 36 bytes, no JSON, no quotes.

patches.why: Every other single-item GET documents a 404. This route documents only 200 and 400, while an unknown routine id returns 404 with {"error": "Routine not found"} as JSON. Observed 2026-08-23, body shape 2026-08-24.

value.description: No routine with this id on this account

patches.why: The 404 declares no content, and the body is the bare string "Workout not found" served as text/html, not JSON. A generated client that parses every error body as JSON throws here. Observed 2026-08-24.

The 404 declares no content, and the body is the bare string "Routine folder not found" served as text/html, not JSON. A generated client that parses every error body as JSON throws here. Observed 2026-08-24.

The 404 declares no content, and the body is the bare string "Exercise template not found" served as text/html, not JSON. A generated client that parses every error body as JSON throws here. Observed 2026-08-24.

The 400 body's error is an object holding an issues array, not the string the spec declares. Every other route that answers {"error": …} sends a string, so a caller cannot treat the field uniformly. Observed 2026-08-24, and with a valid key 2026-11-18.

error.description: A validation report, not a message
